company_name: DHL Group (DHL AG, formerly Deutsche Post AG)

equity_bridge.item: Provisions for pensions and similar obligations
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 balance sheet, 2026-06-30 (EUR 1,660m at FY2025). Pre-tax, conservative.
~EUR 250m/yr NCI profit run-rate (FY2025 205; H1 2026 135 incl. ASMO) x ~13x; book value EUR 528m.

equity_bridge.item: H1 2026 owner FCF already in the 30 June balance sheet
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 FCF EUR 1,658m (H1 report line 583) less ~EUR 90m half-year SBC; Y1 projects all of FY2026, so this removes the double count against the June net debt.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue_5yr_cagr (4.4%) and 10yr revenue CAGR FY2015-25 (3.4%), tempered for a mature, cycle-exposed franchise; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 10.0% diverges >30% from revenue (4.4%) and EPS (5.2%) 5yr CAGRs. It is inflated by the FY2021 pandemic-freight equity jump (13.8bn -> 19.0bn) and then depressed by ~EUR 5bn of buybacks since 2022 (3yr -1.5%); it is not a usable growth proxy.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use owner FCF = DHL-reported FCF (incl. M&A, post-lease, post-interest) less SBC; FY2020 and FY2022 are pandemic/freight-peak years, so negative 3yr/5yr CAGRs measure normalisation from a cyclical peak, not structural decline. Ex-M&A owner FCF rose 7.9% FY2024->FY2025 (2,802 -> 3,024). SBC (0.2% of revenue) is immaterial to the CAGR gap: owner and reported FCF CAGRs differ by <1pp.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 delivers the twice-raised guidance (EBIT > EUR 7.0bn, FCF ex-M&A > EUR 3.2bn) on a ~EUR 89bn revenue base, partly on tight air-freight capacity; FY2027 normalises (revenue +1%, cash EBITDA margin back to ~13.1%) and Strategy 2030 then rebuilds it to 13.5% with ~3% revenue growth. Capex follows guidance (~EUR 3.6bn) and settles at 3.5% of revenue. Owner FCF ~EUR 3.0bn in FY2026, dipping in FY2027, then compounding mid-single digit.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2026 step-up is structural, not cyclical: Express holds its yield and cost gains, Life Sciences & Healthcare and New Energy logistics compound, and the contract-logistics lead wins share in high-growth geographies. Revenue grows 4-5% mid-decade and cash EBITDA margin reaches 14.4% (EBIT margin ~8.2%) with easing capex intensity after the aircraft renewal.
scenario_narratives.bear: The beat reverses: air capacity loosens and freight rates fall (FY2027 revenue -4%), US tariff / de minimis changes and the EU July-2026 customs reform weigh on Express and Forwarding volumes, German mail decline continues, and margin resets to the FY2024 trough (~12.3% cash EBITDA). Capex and lease costs prove sticky, so owner FCF stalls and leverage-funded buybacks have to slow.

valuation_philosophy.summary: DHL is valued as a mature, cyclical, cash-generative logistics operator on strict owner FCF: lease cash, capex and SBC are all charged, leases are treated as an operating cost (DHL's own FCF convention) and excluded from net debt, and NCI and pensions are deducted once in the bridge. Terminal value is capped at 14x terminal owner FCF (cyclical band), below the ~17x a Gordon value at 8%/2% implies, so the valuation does not pay a peak-cycle multiple on peak-cycle FY2026 margins.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin cyclicality: FY2026 cash EBITDA margin (~13.6%) is above the FY2023-25 average (~13.0%); every 0.5pp of sustained margin is ~EUR 0.3bn/yr of pre-tax cash flow.
Lease treatment: switching to treatment (A) without a renewal-capex charge would overstate value by roughly the EUR 15bn lease book; the model charges ~EUR 3.2bn/yr of lease cash in perpetuity.
Capex intensity: guidance has been raised to ~EUR 3.6bn; if 4% of revenue proves the steady state rather than 3.5%, terminal FCF falls ~EUR 0.45bn.
Trade policy (US tariffs/de minimis, EU customs reform) on Express and Forwarding volumes.
NCI valuation is an estimate (earnings multiple on a run-rate boosted by the ASMO consolidation).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 38.76-58.90
data_sources.financials: DHL.DE_Metrics.csv (FY2015-FY2025, H1 2026); DHL Group 2025 Annual Report (free cash flow calculation, ROU depreciation note, lease note, balance sheet); H1 2026 half-year report (net debt table incl. lease liabilities 15,201, pensions 1,560, NCI 528, share capital and treasury shares, diluted weighted shares)
data_sources.qualitative: DHL.DE_Analysis.json (guidance as of preliminary Q3 2026, 2026-10-16; segment, competitive and risk analysis)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 1,150.0m issued less 39.5m treasury = 1,110.5m outstanding (H1 2026 report, note 14), plus ~12.4m dilutive share-plan awards (H1 2026 diluted weighted 1,126.3m vs basic 1,114.0m). The 2017/2025 convertible was repaid in 2025, so no convertible dilution remains. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks (EUR 1,446m FY2025, EUR 561m H1 2026) are the funding mechanism and are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 = EUR 177m (group share-based payment expense, annual report). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line (German plans settle in treasury shares bought in the market; EquityAwardTaxes = 0). About EUR 40m of the total is cash-settled and therefore already inside OCF, so deducting the full 177 slightly over-charges; kept as the conservative basis.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:17Z regular XETRA close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built, flows' own currency. Risk-free 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 (cyclical trade-exposed logistics) -> cost of equity ~8.2-8.5%. Under lease treatment (B) leases are an operating cost, so the capital structure is financial debt + pensions only (~EUR 9bn vs ~EUR 64bn market cap, ~12% weight) at ~2.6% after tax -> ~7.6%. Rounded UP to 8.0% for a cyclical with an A-/A2 rating. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and trade-policy risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash cost (repayment of lease liabilities EUR 2,715m + interest on lease liabilities EUR 719m = EUR 3,434m FY2025, net of EUR 234m lease-receivable receipts = EUR 3,200m, 3.86% of revenue; H1 2026 ~3.7%) charged through lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT. D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 4,867 less ROU depreciation 2,426 = 2,441, 2.95% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice and cash-tax EBIT is correct. Lease liabilities (EUR 15,201m at 2026-06-30) EXCLUDED from net debt: net_debt 7,523 = DHL-defined net debt 22,724 less lease liabilities 15,201. This matches DHL's own FCF definition, which also deducts lease cash.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at an earnings-based value (NCI profit EUR 205m FY2025, EUR 135m H1 2026 after full consolidation of Saudi JV ASMO from mid-2025; ~EUR 250m/yr run-rate x ~13x = EUR 3,200m), not at the EUR 528m book value, which understates it.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 2: operating company, non-US, cyclical; material IFRS 16 leases; NCI). DHL is an operating logistics group (Express, Global Forwarding/Freight, Supply Chain, eCommerce, Post & Parcel Germany) -- none of the bank/REIT/holdco rows apply. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). BASE FLOW: DHL's own 'free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures' FY2025 EUR 3,201m (OCF 9,119 - net capex 2,680 - net lease cash 3,200 - net interest 38), less SBC 177 = owner FCF EUR 3,024m. Interest income is NOT stripped: DHL is net debt, not net cash; the EUR 38m net interest inside the reported figure is immaterial. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is a CASH adjusted EBITDA margin = (IFRS EBITDA + SBC)/revenue less 0.2pp for structural operating cash leakage (provision utilisation, other non-cash items; OCF - (EBITDA - cash tax) averaged ~EUR 0.3bn/yr FY2023-25). FY2025: (10,970 + 177)/82,855 = 13.45% -> 13.25% cash. Only 0.2pp (not the full ~0.38pp) is taken because pension provisions are deducted as a stock in the bridge. Equity-method income (Evri 30% stake etc., EUR 61m FY2025) is inside EBIT, so the EUR 875m equity-method carrying value is NOT added to the bridge. FY2026 GUIDANCE (raised 2026-10-16 on preliminary Q3): Group EBIT > EUR 7.0bn, FCF ex-M&A > EUR 3.2bn, capex ~EUR 3.6bn; mid-term EBIT > EUR 7bn to be reviewed March 2027. Year-1 base calibrated to that: revenue ~EUR 89bn (+7.5%; H1 +5.3%, Q3 ~+12%), cash adj EBITDA 13.6%, capex 4.0%. TIMING: Y1 = FY2026 in full, but the 2026-06-30 balance sheet already contains H1 2026 cash generation (FCF EUR 1,658m less ~EUR 90m half-year SBC); that EUR 1,570m is backed out in equity_bridge so H1 is not counted twice. Post-June buybacks (Tranche X to 31 Aug 2026) are value-neutral and ignored.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in EUR, XETRA quote in EUR; no conversion (fx_rate 1.0).

bear.narrative: The 2026 beat was mostly the transient air-capacity squeeze: FY2027 revenue falls 4% as air and ocean rates normalise and tariff / de minimis / EU customs-reform shocks hit Express and Forwarding volumes, German letter mail keeps shrinking under VAT-distorted competition, and thin-margin Forwarding (~4% EBIT) drags. Cash EBITDA margin resets to ~12.3% (FY2024-like trough) and stays there; capex stays sticky at 3.7% of a smaller base and lease costs drift up, so owner FCF stalls around EUR 2.3-2.6bn.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on raised guidance (EBIT > EUR 7.0bn, FCF ex-M&A > EUR 3.2bn) helped by tight air-freight capacity; FY2027 gives some back as air capacity loosens and freight rates normalise (revenue +1%, cash EBITDA margin 13.1%, near the FY2023-25 average); Strategy 2030 / Fit for Growth then lifts margin ~0.1pp/yr to 13.5% (EBIT margin ~7.5%, roughly the mid-term > EUR 7bn target on a growing base). Capex stays elevated at the guided ~EUR 3.6bn before settling at 3.5% of revenue.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guided ~EUR 3.6bn gross (~4.0% of ~EUR 89bn revenue, net of ~0.1bn disposals); history net capex 3.2-4.6% of revenue FY2021-25.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Cash taxes / lease-adjusted EBIT: FY2023 ~31%, FY2024 30.5%, FY2025 23.5% (low year); H1 2026 cash tax EUR 695m annualises to ~25% of expected EBIT. Ramp to 27% (below the 30.5% group effective GAAP rate because financial interest and pension costs are deductible but sit outside this EBIT).

bull.narrative: The 2026 step-up proves structural: Express keeps the yield and cost gains after air capacity normalises, Life Sciences & Healthcare (CRYOPDP, SDS) and New Energy compound, and Supply Chain's ~2x-share lead in contract logistics wins outsourcing in Mexico, India and the Middle East. Revenue grows 4-5% mid-decade, cash EBITDA margin climbs to 14.4% (EBIT margin ~8.2%, between FY2022 and FY2021 levels) and capex intensity eases as the aircraft renewal completes.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because FY2026 earnings carry a transient air-capacity tailwind management itself flags, the mid-term target is up for review in March 2027, and Express/Forwarding volumes are exposed to policy-driven trade shocks. Base 50% as the guided path. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things -- the cyclical gain persisting AND Strategy 2030 margin expansion beyond the FY2022 level -- with the price already near its 52-week high.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
